summary: This Restaurant class holds a single method that turns a numeric spice rating from 1 to 5 into a readable description such as "Mild" or "Spicy", and reports anything outside that range as invalid.

lines.text: The class acts as a container for restaurant-related behaviour; it has no main method, so it is meant to be compiled and called from other code such as a test.
The method takes an int and hands back a String, which is the whole point of the exercise: converting a number the kitchen uses into words a diner understands.

This is a switch expression rather than a switch statement, so the whole switch evaluates to one value that is returned immediately. Because every branch produces a String, no temporary variable is needed.
The arrow form pairs a label with the value it produces, and unlike old-style case labels it does not fall through to the next branch, so no break is required.
The middle of the scale sits exactly halfway between mild and spicy, which keeps the five labels evenly balanced.
A switch expression must produce a value for every possible input, so default is mandatory here; it also guards against 0, negatives, and numbers above 5.
